ai.title: CLI accepts project directory as first argument
ai.summary: The CLI now takes the project directory as its first argument instead of a user prompt. `initProjectRoot` resolves the provided path or defaults to `process.cwd()`, setting the internal `projectRoot` before context loading. This removes the initial prompt handling from `manicode`, requiring users to specify the working directory explicitly when launching via `npm start` or `ts-node`.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant, you now tell it which folder your project lives in first, instead of starting with a question or command. The startup scripts have been changed so the folder path is the first thing you pass when launching, and the program uses that to find your files before it begins loading your project. This is a small internal change for how the tool is launched, and it is live today.

ai.title: Replace flat file list with recursive tree structure in system prompt
ai.summary: Project context generation now builds a recursive `FileTreeNode` structure instead of a flat array of file paths. The system prompt renders this tree using tab-indented hierarchy, improving spatial understanding of the codebase. `common/src/util/file.ts` defines the new schema, while `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` implements the directory traversal and gitignore filtering (including `.git`). `knowledge.md` adds constraints regarding `src` path inclusion and token limits.

eli5.text: When the assistant reviews your project, it now shows you a nested folder-style view of your files instead of a long flat list. So instead of seeing every file path lined up one after another, you see them arranged like a tree, making it easier to understand which files sit inside which directories. This affects how the assistant presents your project's structure when it's working on it. If you looked at the prompt the assistant receives, you'd notice the file listing now uses indentation to show hierarchy rather than listing paths at the same level.

ai.title: npm package version bump to 1.0.21
ai.summary: Incremented `manicode` package version from 1.0.20 to 1.0.21 in `npm-app/package.json`. This change reflects a standard internal release process. No functional code changes or user-facing features are included in this specific diff.

eli5.text: The app's version number was quietly bumped from one minor release to the next as part of a routine internal update. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping: no new features, no fixes, and nothing you would see change in the app. Nothing about your experience is different today, and this update will not affect how you use the app.

ai.title: Improve expand-based diff prompt
ai.summary: Refactored `expandNewContent` in `generate-diffs-via-expansion.ts` to use `createFileBlock` for consistent file formatting and added few-shot examples to the prompt. The extraction logic now trims whitespace and appends a newline instead of blindly slicing the first character. Updates cover backend diff generation and associated tests.

eli5.text: Our system that figures out how to edit code files now gets a clearer, more detailed set of instructions when it tries to piece together what the edited file should look like. Instead of just seeing the file changes, it's now shown a couple of examples of how it should format its response and explain what changed, which helps it produce cleaner, more consistent results. This affects how the system processes code edits in the background. You wouldn't see this directly, but if you were reviewing the system's work, the explanations and final file output would be more uniform and complete.

ai.title: Fix extra space in graph.js test
ai.summary: Removed extra space in `backend/src/__tests__/__mock-data__/graph/expected.ts` and `old.ts`. Updated `CLAUDE_CALL_TIMEOUT` to 200s in `diff-prompt.test.ts`. Changed `it.only` to `it` for graph test.

eli5.text: The test that checks whether the assistant's code-suggestions match the expected output was failing only because of a single stray space character in its reference data. The stray space was stripped out so the comparison passes cleanly. This is internal housekeeping for the test suite and does not change any feature you use.

ai.title: Add fallback for cwd failure in config
ai.summary: Wrap process.cwd() in try/catch within npm-app/src/config.ts to handle deleted working directories. Fallback uses __dirname with warning, or throws if unavailable. Bump manicode version to 1.0.23 in npm-app/package.json.

eli5.text: The tool now handles a rare situation where it loses track of which folder you're working in (for example, if that folder was deleted while the tool was running). Instead of crashing, it falls back to using its own installation folder while warning you, so your tasks can keep going. This only matters in that edge case; in normal use you won't see any difference.

ai.title: System prompt: Execute terminal commands without commentary
ai.summary: backend/src/system-prompt.ts updated to instruct the agent to execute user-provided terminal commands and print results directly, suppressing extra commentary unless analysis is expected. This refines the response format guidelines for internal system behavior. The change applies to the backend system prompt configuration.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to run a terminal command, it now executes that command and shows you the result right away without any extra explanation, stopping only when you need analysis. This means you get the raw output of your command directly, without the assistant adding commentary or asking follow-up questions, making the interaction faster and more straightforward for technical tasks. This behavior is now live today for anyone using the backend system that processes these requests.

ai.title: Fix terminal tool to always pass stdout and stderr
ai.summary: Updated `handleRunTerminalCommand` in `npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts` to return a combined `<terminal_command_result>` containing both `<stdout>` and `<stderr>`, removing the previous logic that short-circuited and returned `<terminal_command_error>` if `stderr` was present. This ensures the model receives standard output even when commands write to standard error. The change applies to the terminal tool handler.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to run a command in a terminal, it now always reports back BOTH what the command printed as normal output AND any error messages it produced, instead of stopping and only showing the error when something went wrong. This means you'll see the full picture of what happened during the command. It affects the internal tool the assistant uses to interact with the terminal.

ai.title: Remove dirname fallback in getCurrentDirectory
ai.summary: Removes the `__dirname` fallback in `getCurrentDirectory` within `npm-app/src/config.ts`. Previously, the function caught `process.cwd()` errors and used `__dirname` as a fallback before throwing. Now, any failure to get the current working directory immediately throws an Error with the original cause, simplifying the error handling flow.

eli5.text: If the system couldn't tell which folder you're working in, it used to quietly switch to a fallback folder and keep going. Now, that situation will immediately produce an error message identifying the problem instead of silently using a different location. Internally, the code that tries to figure out your current folder no longer catches and recovers from failures. This only changes what happens in a rare edge case where your current folder can't be read, and you'd notice it if you triggered that error.

ai.title: manicode 1.0.24
ai.summary: Bumped manicode version 1.0.23 to 1.0.24 in npm-app/package.json. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: The AI assistant app quietly updated its own build number from 1.0.23 to 1.0.24, like a car rolling off the factory line with a slightly newer serial number after routine maintenance. This small internal change doesn't add new features or fix visible problems; it's just a behind-the-scenes step in the regular process of releasing software updates. You, as a user, wouldn't see or feel any difference from this update.

ai.title: system-prompt.ts adds read more files guidance
ai.summary: The system prompt in backend/src/system-prompt.ts was updated to instruct the agent to read a broad range of files for context before acting. It specifies reading 10 more files than deemed most useful and considering all files in the target directory. The <code_review> block requirement now applies after reading files rather than just code files.

eli5.text: The assistant that builds and edits software projects, is now being told to read a broader set of files before making changes, specifically 10 more files than it initially thinks is important, plus all files in the directory it's working in, and then any files those imported. This is an internal adjustment to how the assistant forms its understanding before acting, so people working with it may notice it asks about or references a wider range of project context early in the process.

ai.title: Suppress file and directory read errors in project tree
ai.summary: Commented out `console.error` calls for file processing and directory reading in `npm-app/src/project-files.ts`. Errors are ignored to prevent noise from permission issues during tree generation. Import statements for `common/util/file` were also reformatted.

eli5.text: When the system builds a map of your project's files, it no longer shows error messages if some files or folders are unreadable due to permission restrictions. Instead of printing warnings about files you lack access to, it silently skips them and continues. This means a cleaner output without distracting errors when scanning projects with mixed access levels. The change is live today and affects anyone generating project file trees internally.

ai.title: Add --help flag and clarify project directory in CLI
ai.summary: Added --help and -h flags to the CLI entry point in index.ts, printing usage instructions and exiting cleanly. The startup message now explicitly states the resolved project directory where files will be read and written, replacing the generic prompt in cli.ts. initProjectRoot in project-files.ts was updated to return the resolved path to support this logging. Input handling in cli.ts was also patched to prevent processing user lines while the menu is active.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant, it now tells you exactly which folder it will read and write files from, so you know where your work lives. You can also type a help command to see how to run it and what it does before you begin. While a menu is open, the assistant no longer reacts to keys you type by accident, preventing the wrong action from firing. This is live today for anyone running the assistant from their terminal.

ai.title: Manicode 1.0.27 README restructure
ai.summary: npm-app/README.md reorganized with explicit Features, Knowledge Files, Tips, and Feedback sections. CLI usage updated to `manicode [project-directory]` with default current-directory fallback. Keyboard shortcuts `Ctrl+U`/`Ctrl+R` added for file change undo/redo. Package version bumped to 1.0.27 in npm-app/package.json.

eli5.text: The assistant's instructions guide has been reorganized so you can quickly find what you need, with clear sections for features, knowledge files, tips, and feedback. If you tell the assistant to start in a specific folder, it will; otherwise, it will begin in whatever folder your computer is currently looking at. You can now press Ctrl+U to take back a file change and Ctrl+R to redo it, just like undoing and redoing edits. Behind the scenes, the version number was updated to reflect this new release.
